scenes.tts: If B M P makes skin, what should the organizer make to turn ectoderm neural?
scenes.caption: If BMP makes skin, what should the organizer make to turn ectoderm neural?
scenes.visual: Title card: The Organizer's Catchers. The organizer on the gastrula map, with a question mark.
scenes.narration: If BMP makes skin, what should the organizer make to turn ectoderm neural?

scenes.tts: Something that blocks B M P. It makes at least three such proteins.
scenes.caption: Something that blocks BMP. It makes at least three such proteins.
scenes.visual: Three protein shapes leave the organizer: Noggin, Chordin, Follistatin.
scenes.narration: Something that blocks BMP. It makes at least three such proteins.

scenes.tts: First, where they come from. Chordin and Noggin are made early, at the blastula stage, in dorsal animal cells.
scenes.visual: The blastula map: a hollow ball of cells drawn in cross-section, animal cap at the top shaded as ectoderm, blastocoel inside, endoderm at the floor; beside it a gastrula with the blastopore groove on the lower half, its dorsal lip labeled organizer, dorsal and ventral arrows. Dorsal animal cells of the blastula glow; labels: Chordin, Noggin.
scenes.narration: First, where they come from. Chordin and Noggin are made early, at the blastula stage, in dorsal animal cells.

scenes.tts: So neural induction starts before gastrulation.
scenes.visual: Label: neural induction starts before gastrulation.
scenes.narration: So neural induction starts before gastrulation.

scenes.tts: Then the organizer and dorsal mesoderm turn inward and spread beneath the ectoderm. This is involution.
scenes.visual: Gastrula cross-section: dorsal mesoderm involutes and spreads under the ectoderm. Label: involution.
scenes.narration: Then the organizer and dorsal mesoderm turn inward and spread beneath the ectoderm. This is involution.

scenes.tts: The involuting mesoderm secretes all three. The ectoderm above it becomes the neural plate.
scenes.visual: Antagonist dots rise from the mesoderm into the ectoderm above, which turns blue. Label: neural plate.
scenes.narration: The involuting mesoderm secretes all three. The ectoderm above it becomes the neural plate.

scenes.tts: Noggin was found in nineteen ninety-two by William Smith and Richard Harland. It is a secreted protein made in the organizer.
scenes.caption: Noggin was found in 1992 by William Smith and Richard Harland. It is a secreted protein made in the organizer.
scenes.visual: Label: 1992, Smith and Harland. Noggin protein leaves an organizer cell.
scenes.narration: Noggin was found in 1992 by William Smith and Richard Harland. It is a secreted protein made in the organizer.

scenes.tts: In nineteen ninety-three, Teresa Lamb, Harland and colleagues added Noggin protein to intact caps. What should the caps become?
scenes.caption: In 1993, Teresa Lamb, Harland and colleagues added Noggin protein to intact caps. What should the caps become?
scenes.visual: Label: 1993, Lamb and colleagues. Noggin added to an intact cap. Question on screen.
scenes.narration: In 1993, Teresa Lamb, Harland and colleagues added Noggin protein to intact caps. What should the caps become?

scenes.tts: Neural tissue, without dorsal mesoderm. Noggin acted on the ectoderm directly.
scenes.visual: The cap turns blue; no mesoderm forms. Label: neural, no dorsal mesoderm.
scenes.narration: Neural tissue, without dorsal mesoderm. Noggin acted on the ectoderm directly.

scenes.tts: The markers were all anterior. Forebrain is neural. Cement gland, a mucus gland at the head end, is not.
scenes.visual: Two separate labeled outputs at the head end: blue anterior brain tissue (forebrain) and, beside it, a non-neural cement gland drawn in a different color. Label: cement gland, non-neural.
scenes.narration: The markers were all anterior. Forebrain is neural. Cement gland, a mucus gland at the head end, is not.

scenes.tts: Chordin was cloned in nineteen ninety-four by Yoshiki Sasai and colleagues, in Eddy De Robertis's laboratory.
scenes.caption: Chordin was cloned in 1994 by Yoshiki Sasai and colleagues, in Eddy De Robertis's laboratory.
scenes.visual: Label: 1994, Sasai, De Robertis laboratory. Chordin gene lights in organizer cells.
scenes.narration: Chordin was cloned in 1994 by Yoshiki Sasai and colleagues, in Eddy De Robertis's laboratory.

scenes.tts: Both Noggin and Chordin bind B M P four and keep it off its receptors.
scenes.caption: Both Noggin and Chordin bind BMP4 and keep it off its receptors.
scenes.visual: Noggin and Chordin each grab a BMP4 dimer before it reaches the receptors.
scenes.narration: Both Noggin and Chordin bind BMP4 and keep it off its receptors.

scenes.tts: Folly-statin was known as a protein that binds activin. It also neuralizes caps and binds some B M Ps.
scenes.caption: Follistatin was known as a protein that binds activin. It also neuralizes caps and binds some BMPs.
scenes.visual: Follistatin wraps a ligand. Labels: binds activin; also some BMPs.
scenes.narration: Follistatin was known as a protein that binds activin. It also neuralizes caps and binds some BMPs.

scenes.tts: It works differently. It can stay bound to B M P as B M P docks on its receptor. That complex does not signal.
scenes.caption: It works differently. It can stay bound to BMP as BMP docks on its receptor. That complex does not signal.
scenes.visual: Follistatin, BMP and a receptor drawn together as one three-part complex; the receptor stays dark.
scenes.narration: It works differently. It can stay bound to BMP as BMP docks on its receptor. That complex does not signal.

scenes.tts: None of the three needs to enter a cell. Each grabs B M P outside the cell.
scenes.caption: None of the three needs to enter a cell. Each grabs BMP outside the cell.
scenes.visual: All three antagonists stay outside the membrane; the receptors below them stay dark.
scenes.narration: None of the three needs to enter a cell. Each grabs BMP outside the cell.

scenes.tts: In the crystal structure, Noggin clasps a B M P dimer and covers the faces the receptors would bind.
scenes.caption: In the crystal structure, Noggin clasps a BMP dimer and covers the faces the receptors would bind.
scenes.visual: Structure view: a Noggin dimer clasping a BMP-7 dimer, the receptor faces shaded and covered.
scenes.narration: In the crystal structure, Noggin clasps a BMP dimer and covers the faces the receptors would bind.

scenes.tts: Chordin has a further twist. In the shuttling model, B M P bound to Chordin travels toward the ventral side. There, Tolloid proteases cut Chordin and release the B M P.
scenes.caption: Chordin has a further twist. In the shuttling model, BMP bound to Chordin travels toward the ventral side. There, Tolloid proteases cut Chordin and release the BMP.
scenes.visual: A Chordin-BMP complex drifts ventrally first; only then does a Tolloid protease cut Chordin, and BMP is released there. Label: the shuttling model.
scenes.narration: Chordin has a further twist. In the shuttling model, BMP bound to Chordin travels toward the ventral side. There, Tolloid proteases cut Chordin and release the BMP.

scenes.tts: Caps show what the catchers can do. Does the embryo need them?
scenes.visual: A whole frog embryo replaces the dish. Question on screen: does the embryo need them?
scenes.narration: Caps show what the catchers can do. Does the embryo need them?

scenes.tts: In two thousand five, Khokha and colleagues depleted Chordin, Noggin and Folly-statin together from frog embryos. What happens to the neural plate?
scenes.caption: In 2005, Khokha and colleagues depleted Chordin, Noggin and Follistatin together from frog embryos. What happens to the neural plate?
scenes.visual: Label: 2005, Khokha and colleagues, Xenopus tropicalis. All three antagonists crossed out. Question on screen.
scenes.narration: In 2005, Khokha and colleagues depleted Chordin, Noggin and Follistatin together from frog embryos. What happens to the neural plate?

scenes.tts: The embryos lost their dorsal structures, the neural plate among them. With all three catchers gone, B M P signaling stays high.
scenes.caption: The embryos lost their dorsal structures, the neural plate among them. With all three catchers gone, BMP signaling stays high.
scenes.visual: The embryo's dorsal side stays skin-colored; dorsal structures, including the neural plate, fail to form. Label: dorsal structures lost.
scenes.narration: The embryos lost their dorsal structures, the neural plate among them. With all three catchers gone, BMP signaling stays high.

scenes.tts: The reverse test agreed. Reversade's group removed three B M Ps from embryos whose organizer signals were blocked. The embryos formed massive amounts of brain.
scenes.caption: The reverse test agreed. Reversade's group removed three BMPs from embryos whose organizer signals were blocked. The embryos formed massive amounts of brain.
scenes.visual: Label: Reversade and colleagues. Background label: organizer signals prevented by ultraviolet treatment or beta-catenin knockdown. BMP2, BMP4 and BMP7 crossed out; the embryo turns largely blue with a large brain.
scenes.narration: The reverse test agreed. Reversade's group removed three BMPs from embryos whose organizer signals were blocked. The embryos formed massive amounts of brain.

scenes.tts: Early F G F signaling is also needed in the frog, in addition to blocking B M P. It can turn the dial down through M A P K. It also does more.
scenes.caption: Early FGF signaling is also needed in the frog, in addition to blocking BMP. It can turn the dial down through MAPK. It also does more.
scenes.visual: The Smad1 dial with an FGF arrow feeding the MAPK hand, and a second FGF arrow that bypasses the dial and points straight at the neural fate. Label: FGF, a second input.
scenes.narration: Early FGF signaling is also needed in the frog, in addition to blocking BMP. It can turn the dial down through MAPK. It also does more.

scenes.tts: The takeaway: the frog embryo needs the catchers to keep the dial down. And F G F adds a second input.
scenes.caption: The takeaway: the frog embryo needs the catchers to keep the dial down. And FGF adds a second input.
scenes.visual: A single round dial labeled Smad1 in the nucleus, held low by the three catchers outside the cell, with a separate FGF arrow beside it. Takeaway on screen: the embryo needs the catchers; FGF adds a second input.
scenes.narration: The takeaway: the frog embryo needs the catchers to keep the dial down. And FGF adds a second input.
